verdict: Vistra's profit nearly doubled to $1.1B in a record-hot summer that lifted power prices — helped by $559M of paper gains on hedges for future years.

segments.name: Generation & retail power (combined)
segments.note: All of Vistra's electricity generation and retail sales, combined — Vistra's earnings release does not split revenue by segment (its segment profit split is in the takeaways below); the revenue split by Retail, Texas, East and West arrives with the Form 10-Q.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of power plants and nuclear fuel over their lives — up with the plants acquired from Lotus.

opex.name: Operating costs
opex.note: Running the generation fleet and retail business day to day, excluding fuel.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling power to retail customers and running the company.

opex.name: Impairment of long-lived assets
opex.note: Write-down of long-lived assets, including the partial impairment of the Moss Landing 350 battery facility.

otherDetail: Other income of $44M, less $254M of interest expense and related charges.
oneTimers: $559M of unrealized gains on hedges expected to settle in future years sits inside GAAP net income — paper profit that flatters the headline. Vistra strips unrealized hedge moves out of its adjusted EBITDA.
$269M impairment of long-lived assets, including the partial impairment of the Moss Landing 350 battery facility in California.
footerNote: Segment revenue by Retail/Texas/East/West is disclosed in Vistra's Form 10-Q, which had not been filed as of Nov 7, 2026; the release reports segment Adjusted EBITDA (Retail $98M, Texas $1,227M, East $979M, West $76M, Corporate & other −$2M, Asset Closure −$18M) but not segment revenue, so revenue is shown combined. Net income of $1,140M is before $48M of preferred-stock dividends ($1,092M attributable to common stock).

takeaways.title: Underlying profit jumped 50%
takeaways.text: Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA rose more than 50% to $2,378M — Texas contributed $1,227M and the East $979M — on higher energy and capacity prices, the Lotus plants, and record summer demand in ERCOT and PJM.

takeaways.title: The fleet showed up in the heat
takeaways.text: In one of the hottest third quarters on record, Vistra's fleet ran at nearly 95% commercial availability — exactly when power is worth the most.

takeaways.title: Still buying growth
takeaways.text: In October Vistra closed the Cogentrix acquisition — about 5,500 MW of gas generation — and authorized another $1.5B of share buybacks, taking remaining authorization to about $2.5B.
